html:
By the Treaty of Roskilde in February 1658 Denmark-Norway gave up Scania, Halland, Blekinge and other lands to Sweden, after the Swedish army crossed the frozen straits and threatened Copenhagen.

The Swedish king Charles X Gustav had marched his army over the ice of the Little and Great Belts that winter, a feat no one had thought possible. Denmark had to accept harsh terms. When he attacked again later that year, Copenhagen held out, and in 1660 Denmark won back Bornholm and Trøndelag.

The provinces east of the Sound stayed Swedish and were made Swedish within a few generations. The treaty set the border between Denmark and Sweden that still holds, and gave Sweden one shore of the Sound. The defeat also led to absolute monarchy in Denmark in 1660. It was a high point of the Swedish Empire.
sum: By the Treaty of Roskilde in February 1658 Denmark-Norway gave up Scania, Halland, Blekinge and other lands to Sweden, after the Swedish army crossed the frozen straits and threatened Copenhagen.
